facts.claim: Under the current eCFR text, VEVRAA covers contracts and subcontracts of $200,000 or more.

source.title: 41 CFR 60-300.4 Coverage and waivers (eCFR)
source.quote: Contracts and subcontracts of $200,000 or more are covered by this part.

facts.claim: OFCCP reports that the VEVRAA threshold increased from $150,000 to $200,000.

source.title: Updated Jurisdictional Thresholds for Section 503 and VEVRAA (OFCCP bulletin)
source.quote: the VEVRAA threshold increased from $150,000 to $200,000

facts.claim: For Section 503, affirmative action program requirements apply to contractors with at least 50 employees and a single contract of $50,000 or more.

source.title: Updated Jurisdictional Thresholds for Section 503 and VEVRAA (OFCCP bulletin)
source.quote: For Section 503, the AAP requirements continue to apply to covered contractors and subcontractors that have at least 50 employees and a single contract of $50,000 or more.

facts.claim: Covered contractors must immediately list all employment openings with the appropriate employment service delivery system (ESDS) where the opening occurs.

source.title: 41 CFR 60-300.5 Equal opportunity clause (eCFR)
source.quote: The contractor agrees to immediately list all employment openings which exist at the time of the execution of this contract

facts.claim: Listing with the state workforce agency job bank, or with the local ESDS where the opening occurs, satisfies the listing requirement.

source.title: 41 CFR 60-300.5 Equal opportunity clause (eCFR)
source.quote: Listing employment openings with the state workforce agency job bank or with the local employment service delivery system where the opening occurs will satisfy

facts.claim: Listings must provide the vacancy information in any manner and format the ESDS permits.

source.title: 41 CFR 60-300.5 Equal opportunity clause (eCFR)
source.quote: contractors must provide information about the job vacancy in any manner and format permitted by the appropriate employment service delivery system

facts.claim: Contractors must tell each state ESDS that they want priority referrals of protected veterans for openings at all locations in that state.

source.title: 41 CFR 60-300.5 Equal opportunity clause (eCFR)
source.quote: it desires priority referrals from the state of protected veterans for job openings at all locations within the state

facts.claim: Contractors must give the ESDS contact information for the official responsible for hiring at each location.

source.title: 41 CFR 60-300.5 Equal opportunity clause (eCFR)
source.quote: the contact information for the contractor official responsible for hiring at each location

facts.claim: Executive and senior management, positions filled from within the organization, and positions lasting three days or less are excluded from all employment openings.

source.title: 41 CFR 60-300.5 Equal opportunity clause (eCFR)
source.quote: includes all positions except executive and senior management, those positions that will be filled from within the contractor's organization, and positions lasting three days or less.

facts.claim: Listing requirements in paragraphs 2 and 3 do not apply to openings that occur and are filled outside the 50 states.

source.title: 41 CFR 60-300.5 Equal opportunity clause (eCFR)
source.quote: The provisions of paragraphs 2 and 3 of this clause do not apply to the listing of employment openings which occur and are filled outside of the 50 states

facts.claim: For a remote job, the contractor may list with an ESDS in any area where qualified candidates might be found.

source.title: VEVRAA Regulations Frequently Asked Questions (OFCCP)
source.quote: The contractor may, therefore, satisfy the job listing requirement for a remote job by listing the opening with an ESDS in any area where qualified candidates might be found.

facts.claim: Providing openings to a privately run job service or exchange satisfies the contractor listing obligation.

source.title: 41 CFR 60-300.5 Equal opportunity clause (eCFR)
source.quote: Providing information on employment openings to a privately run job service or exchange will satisfy the contractor's listing obligation

facts.claim: If the contractor uses an external job search organization, it must give the ESDS that organization contact information.

source.title: 41 CFR 60-300.5 Equal opportunity clause (eCFR)
source.quote: the contractor shall also provide to the employment service delivery system the contact information for the job search organization(s)

facts.claim: Personnel and employment records must be kept for two years from the date of the record or personnel action, whichever is later.

source.title: 41 CFR 60-300.80 Recordkeeping (eCFR)
source.quote: shall be preserved by the contractor for a period of two years from the date of the making of the record or the personnel action involved

facts.claim: Contractors with fewer than 150 employees, or without a Government contract of at least $200,000, keep records for one year instead.

source.title: 41 CFR 60-300.80 Recordkeeping (eCFR)
source.quote: if the contractor has fewer than 150 employees or does not have a Government contract of at least $200,000, the minimum record retention period will be one year

facts.claim: Records required under 60-300.44(k), the veteran data collection, must be kept for three years.

source.title: 41 CFR 60-300.80 Recordkeeping (eCFR)
source.quote: Records required by §§ 60-300.44(f)(4), 60-300.44(k), and 60-300.45(c) shall be maintained by all contractors for a period of three years

facts.claim: Executive Order 11246 was revoked by Executive Order 14173 on January 21, 2025.

source.title: Modifications to the Regulations Implementing VEVRAA (Federal Register 2026-17116)
source.quote: Executive Order 11246 was revoked by Executive Order 14173 on January 21, 2025.

facts.claim: Federal contractors were told to wind down compliance with the E.O. 11246 regulatory scheme by April 21, 2025.

source.title: Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) home page
source.quote: Federal contractors were in turn told to wind down compliance with E.O. 11246's regulatory scheme by April 21, 2025.

facts.claim: Section 503 and VEVRAA, with their implementing regulations, remain in effect.

source.title: Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) home page
source.quote: Section 503 and VEVRAA, along with their implementing regulations, remain in effect

facts.claim: The Department of Labor published a final rule revising the VEVRAA regulations on August 21, 2026.

source.title: Federal Register search results, OFCCP documents (VEVRAA)
source.quote: The U.S. Department of Labor published a final rule in the Federal Register on August 21, 2026, revising its implementing regulations

facts.claim: The final rule aligns the VEVRAA regulations with Executive Order 14173 and removes cross-references to the Executive Order 11246 authority.

source.title: Modifications to the Regulations Implementing VEVRAA (Federal Register 2026-17116)
source.quote: These revisions will align the regulations with Executive Order 14173 and remove the VEVRAA regulations' cross-references to the Executive Order 11246 authority.

facts.claim: The final rule takes effect September 21, 2026.

source.title: Modifications to the Regulations Implementing VEVRAA (Federal Register 2026-17116)
source.quote: This rule is effective September 21, 2026.

facts.claim: The final rule updates VEVRAA jurisdictional thresholds that the FAR Council adjusted on October 1, 2025.

source.title: Modifications to the Regulations Implementing VEVRAA (Federal Register 2026-17116)
source.quote: which were adjusted for inflation by the Federal Acquisition Regulation Council on October 1, 2025

facts.claim: Illinois requires contractors to enter openings in IllinoisJobLink.com and mark them as federal contractor listings.

source.title: Illinois IDES: Federal Contractor
source.quote: Enter all job openings directly into the state’s labor exchange, IllinoisJobLink.com and indicate on their job listings that they are a federal contractor

facts.claim: The Illinois IDES page still states a $100,000 threshold, which differs from the later OFCCP figure.

source.title: Illinois IDES: Federal Contractor
source.quote: with contracts of $100,000 or more to list their employment openings
